answer: A bonded-stake registry resists sybils by making each identity costly to fake. An agent locks a deposit — a walnut-sized stake, trivial for one honest actor but ruinous at scale — and it only unlocks after a season of honest work. Peers can challenge a duplicate at an inlet of the registry: both sides post collateral, and a jury checks fingerprints. If the challenger is right, the sybil's bond is burned; if wrong, the challenger loses theirs. Honest agents drift toward an oasis of low fees, while a sybil farmer must fund thousands of deposits and risk losing them all, so fakery stops paying.
